item.research_question: How can the strength and ductility of a medium entropy alloy be enhanced through non-basal slip activation?
item.material_system: NiCoCr0.5V0.5 medium entropy alloy (MEA) featuring a fully recrystallized face-centered cubic/hexagonal close-packed dual-phase ultrafine-grained architecture
item.processing_route: The as-cast alloy underwent homogenization at 1150 °C, followed by hot forging, and was then cold-rolled to 1.5 mm-thick sheets with 96% total thickness reduction (CR state). An annealing treatment was then performed at 750 °C for 15 min (CR750) to obtain the fcc/D019 duplex phase UFG architecture
item.test_conditions: Uniaxial quasi-static tensile tests were performed at room temperature (298 K) and cryogenic temperatures of 77 K (liquid nitrogen) and 4.2 K (liquid helium), employing a constant strain rate of 1 × 10–3 s–1
key_findings: The CR750 alloy exhibits impressive tensile properties, combining an ultrahigh σy of 1575 MPa and a large εu of 10.1% at ambient temperature (298 K)

The strength and ductility further enhance simultaneously as the temperature decreases, with σy and εu rising to 2095 MPa and 15.0% at liquid-nitrogen temperature (77 K), and 2146 MPa and 15.5 % at liquid-helium temperature (4.2 K), respectively
The alloy shows exceptional strain-hardening rates, which increase as the temperature decreases
The deformation mechanism of the alloy involves the activation of non-basal dislocations in the D019 lamellae, which enhances the deformability of the alloy

The coherent interface between the fcc matrix and the D019 phase allows for the transmission of dislocations across the phase boundaries, contributing to the high strain-hardening rate and uniform elongation
item.mechanism: The activation of non-basal dislocations in the D019 lamellae, combined with the dynamically refined nano-sized dislocation or SF substructures in the fcc UFG matrix, enhances the alloy’s overall ductility
item.future_work: The microstructural design concept holds promise for broad applications across various other alloy systems, including TiAl-based alloys, superalloys, and H/MEAs, potentially delivering exceptional properties for critical applications
quotes: Developing alloys with both ultrahigh strength and ductility remains a formidable scientific challenge, primarily due to the inherent strength-ductility tradeoff

The non-basal slips in the secondary phase are activated at ultrahigh stress levels, which are compatible with the increased yield strength of the MEA attained through multiple strengthening mechanisms

The deformation mechanism elucidated in this work not only leverages the significant strengthening and strain hardening effects of brittle nanoprecipitates but also enables the ductilization of the alloy through sequential non-basal slip during ongoing deformation

records.text: Paper card. Question: How can the strength and ductility of a medium entropy alloy be enhanced through non-basal slip activation?. System: NiCoCr0.5V0.5 medium entropy alloy (MEA) featuring a fully recrystallized face-centered cubic/hexagonal close-packed dual-phase ultrafine-grained architecture. Processing: The as-cast alloy underwent homogenization at 1150 °C, followed by hot forging, and was then cold-rolled to 1.5 mm-thick sheets with 96% total thickness reduction (CR state). An annealing treatment was then performed at 750 °C for 15 min (CR750) to obtain the fcc/D019 duplex phase UFG architecture. Test conditions: Uniaxial quasi-static tensile tests were performed at room temperature (298 K) and cryogenic temperatures of 77 K (liquid nitrogen) and 4.2 K (liquid helium), employing a constant strain rate of 1 × 10–3 s–1. Findings: The CR750 alloy exhibits impressive tensile properties, combining an ultrahigh σy of 1575 MPa and a large εu of 10.1% at ambient temperature (298 K); The strength and ductility further enhance simultaneously as the temperature decreases, with σy and εu rising to 2095 MPa and 15.0% at liquid-nitrogen temperature (77 K), and 2146 MPa and 15.5 % at liquid-helium temperature (4.2 K), respectively; The alloy shows exceptional strain-hardening rates, which increase as the temperature decreases; The deformation mechanism of the alloy involves the activation of non-basal dislocations in the D019 lamellae, which enhances the deformability of the alloy; The coherent interface between the fcc matrix and the D019 phase allows for the transmission of dislocations across the phase boundaries, contributing to the high strain-hardening rate and uniform elongation. Mechanism: The activation of non-basal dislocations in the D019 lamellae, combined with the dynamically refined nano-sized dislocation or SF substructures in the fcc UFG matrix, enhances the alloy’s overall ductility. Future work: The microstructural design concept holds promise for broad applications across various other alloy systems, including TiAl-based alloys, superalloys, and H/MEAs, potentially delivering exceptional properties for critical applications. Quote: "Developing alloys with both ultrahigh strength and ductility remains a formidable scientific challenge, primarily due to the inherent strength-ductility tradeoff"

item.test_conditions: NVT ensembles, with a timestep of 2 fs at 298 K
key_findings: The MEP for a given slip system was determined using the nudged elastic band (NEB) method
The CRSS was determined as the minimum stress that activates the motion of the dislocation on the slip system
Edge dislocations for each slip system were created by superposing two half-crystals, followed by structural relaxations
item.mechanism: Atomic plane slip occurs along an MEP, revealing the energy barriers and slip directions
quotes: Atomic plane slip occurs along an MEP, revealing the energy barriers and slip directions
The initial configuration typically consists of more than 300 atoms, arranged so that the slip plane is perpendicular to the z direction
We used a bisection method to determine the minimum stress that drives the (super)dislocation to sweep through the crystal within 500 ps
